chapter_meta_description: Han Li navigates the Lava Path’s black desert with Yuan Yao, but the real storm is the Star Palace elders’ cold confession: they unleashed the Iron Fire Ants to cull a generation of Core Formation cultivators and bluff their way through a political crisis.
og_title: Ch. 472 – The Star Palace’s Bloody Bluff
og_description: Han Li survives the Lava Path’s black desert swarms while hidden elders admit to engineering a massacre. The Void Heaven Palace trials are a political slaughterhouse.
twitter_title: RMJI Ch. 472: The Lava Path Massacre Was No Accident
twitter_description: Star Palace elders confess to deploying Iron Fire Ants and Silver Light Rats in a calculated bid to cull Core Formation elites and bluff their way through a succession crisis.

lore_anchors.definition: A gem-like artifact refined from the soul of a ghostly beast; it allows the bearer to command a bound spirit beast without personally refining the beast’s original soul imprint.
A rare spirit beast with an innate ability to suppress evil spirits and soul-based attacks; its exact origins and full capabilities remain partially unknown even to its handlers.
A terrain hazard on the Lava Path that appeared for the first time in this expedition; characterized by scorching black sand and swarms of deadly Iron Fire Ants.
A ferocious flying insect that is immune to ordinary magical treasure attacks, spits black fire, and can combine into tactical formations; deployed as a high-tier restriction by the Star Palace.
One branch of the Ice Fire Path’s second trial; a hazardous zone of blood-red ice pillars infested with Silver Light Rats and other ice-aligned threats.
A silver-furred rodent with a single, short silver horn on its head; it attacks in swarms, using its horn to deliver thunderous impacts, and is another Star Palace-controlled restriction.
A secret, high-power fire-thunder artifact from the demonic sect Qing Yang Gate; its power rivals a Nascent Soul cultivator’s Primordial Yang Fire and was used by Yuan Yao to escape the ant swarm.
A unique, supreme technique possessed by the Star Palace’s two Saint Masters; it is so fearsome that even top-tier Nascent Soul cultivators avoid a direct confrontation with it.

The supreme treasure sealed within the innermost chamber of the Void Heaven Palace; the primary target of the orthodox and demonic expeditions; its retrieval is the unspoken prize that all factions are maneuvering for.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Star Palace suddenly unleash such deadly swarms?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are bluffing. With their two Saint Masters unreachable in seclusion, the elders hope to cull a huge number of Core Formation elites from enemy sects, making those factions hesitate and think the Star Palace is still overwhelmingly strong.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why don’t the orthodox and demonic sects just attack the Star Palace afterward?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because their real goal is the Void Heaven Cauldron, not justice. As the cold-voiced elder points out, they won’t go to war over lost rank-and-file disciples who aren’t even their personal successors.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the Primordial Magnetic Light?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A supreme technique unique to the Star Palace’s two Saint Masters. In the novel’s power scale, it is so dominant that top Nascent Soul cultivators like the madwoman of Ten Thousand Methods Sect and Six Paths of Sacred Devil Island would retreat rather than fight it head-on.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Yuan Yao lying about the Soul-Collecting Bead’s side effects?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Almost certainly. Han Li catches her evasiveness immediately and decides to accept the bead but never refine it—classic mortal-stream behavior: secure the asset, investigate the danger later.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Azure Robe Scholar worry about “that brat surnamed Han”?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The scholar has a vested interest in Han Li’s survival, likely tied to their earlier arrangement or shared goals within the Void Heaven Palace. His anxiety confirms that the abnormal trial conditions are lethal even for a prepared Core Formation cultivator.
